svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reference figure for genre `bitfield` — NORMATIVE surface only (spec/genres/bitfield.md). # Every construct here is inside the v0.1 conformance surface and the # compatibility promise. This genre reaches NO experimental construct at all # `stroke=` was promoted to NORMATIVE (`STROKE-KEY-STATUS`) and `color=` # was retired (`COLOUR-KEY-STATUS`), which were the only two it could ever reach, so # bitfield-experimental.fd was deleted rather than left empty. # The set demonstrates every FORM of every keyword, not just every keyword. # Coverage: node tools/reference-coverage.js --normative-only --strict bitfield figdown 0.1 bitfield title "Telemetry export framing"
# `class` declares a meaning ONCE; elements join it with class=. The meaning # string is required — it is what a reading agent gets instead of a hex value. # `style=` is NOT among them here: it cannot reach a field by ANY route. # It left `field`'s own option list (`STYLE-KEY-SCOPE`), and a class that # declares it is silently ignored on a field member while the legend still # draws the dash — a swatch for ink no field can carry. `tools/legend-check.js` # is the gate for that; this class uses `stroke=`, which does reach. class vendor "Vendor-defined — not interoperable" stroke=#7c3aed class present "Present only when the C flag is set" fill=#fef3c7 class reserved "Reserved — senders write zero" fill=#e7e5e4
# `numbering=` is REQUIRED and has NO default (`UNSAFE-DEFAULT-ELIMINATION`). msb0 is the IETF packet # convention: bit 0 is the MSB, ruler 0…N-1 left to right. A defaulted # direction would render a ruler asserting something false, and a wrong ruler # looks exactly like a right one. `word=` is the row width in bits; 32 is also # the default, written here so the reader need not know that to read the rows. bitfield hdr "Export header (on the wire)" word=32 numbering=msb0 # Classic form. The name is a WHITESPACE-delimited position, so `QUOTING-RULES` requires # quotes even when the name contains no space: `field Ver 4` is a line error. field "Ver" 4 # `description=` is authored documentation prose (IEEE 1685's spelling; it was # `note=` until this release). It is in the MODEL but its only ink is an SVG # <title> tooltip, so a fact a human must SEE belongs in the label or in a # class meaning instead. §12.7 lets an agent quote or display it, never parse it. field "Header Length" 6 description="in 32-bit words; minimum 3" field "Flags" 6 class=vendor # `present=` is "present only if", not "variable width": the width is fixed and # only the presence is not, so a reader computing offsets ACROSS it must branch # and emit both offset sets (`BITFIELD-CONDITIONAL-OFFSETS`). The renderer dashes it, and a STATED # condition also draws a caption under the block. Both written forms are here: # `present="…"` (condition stated) on Checksum, `present=""` (conditional, # condition NOT stated — the author claimed nothing) on Sequence. field "Checksum" 16 present="the C flag is set" class=present # The dash IS `present=` and nothing can clear it: `style=` left `field` # entirely (`STYLE-KEY-SCOPE`) because `style=solid` used to erase the dash # while the model still recorded the field as conditionally present — one line, # two different figures for a human and for a reading agent (`PRESENTATION-AS-MEANING-CARRIER`). field "Sequence" 32 present="" # Wider than `word=`: the field spans the following rows automatically and is # still ONE field — one box, name written once. Splitting it into per-row # pieces would assert two fields on the wire that do not exist. field "Export Timestamp" 64 fill=#dbeafe # class= takes a comma-separated LIST. The channels apply left to right and # the later class wins per channel; here they touch different channels, so the # fill comes from `reserved` and the outline colour from `vendor`. field "Pad" 8 class=reserved,vendor # `break` ends the drawing row explicitly. It is presentation only: it adds, # skips and reorders no bits, and the blank cells it leaves are NOT bits. It # needs a field declared since the block opened or since the previous break. break # `*` fills the remainder of the current row — the variable-length tail. At # most one per block, and the budget is per BLOCK, so `tlv` below has its own. field "Records" * description="record count derived from Header Length"
# The `Records` region above, expanded — one record, in a block of its own # with its own ruler; the same device examples/srh.fd uses for the SRH's # Flags octet. This block is where `index=` lives (`BITFIELD-REPETITION-CONSTRUCT`), and it # needs a repeated structure to live in: the key says a `field` is ONE # ELEMENT of a repeated run, and before it existed a run had to be written as # N literal `field` lines, which put N objects in the model and so ASSERTED a # cardinality the wire does not have. All three written forms are below, and # they are a tri-state with the same shape as `present=`'s: an ABSENT key # claims nothing at all — it is NOT a claim that the field occurs once — # `index=""` claims repetition and states no index, and a range states one. bitfield rec "Export record (one entry of the Records region)" word=32 numbering=msb0 field "Entry Count" 16 description="flow entries in this record; the entries are numbered from 1" # DETERMINATE: both ends are literal integers, so the run is |last-first|+1 = # 8 elements and the count is IN the document. Quotes are inert here (RULE # 2.3) — `index="0..7"` says exactly what this line says, because determinacy # is decided by parsing both ends and never by quoting. Descent needs no key # of its own: `index=7..0` is the same eight gauges counted the other way. field "Queue Depth" 16 index=0..7 # …and that is what a determinate run buys: this field's offset is still # computable — 16 + 8×16 = 144 bits in — even though only TWO of the eight # elements above are DRAWN (the first and the last, `REPEATED-RUN-DRAWING`). The elision strip # between them occupies NO bit positions, so a # reader who counts drawn cells is reading the drawing (`MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE`) and will get # this offset wrong; the count comes from `index=`, never from the picture. field "Drop Count" 32 # PROSE last index: the count is in `Entry Count` on the wire and NOT in this # document, so the run is indeterminate and so is every offset after it — but # that is now reached from SYNTAX rather than from a reader recognising a # label. The prose is never parsed or resolved: an agent may quote and # display "Entry Count" and MUST NOT match it to the field of that name # (§12.7, the locator problem). `<first>` is ALWAYS a literal integer, and # that is what lets a 1-based run be drawn 1-based — the canonical form is # 0-based, from the C indexing semantics of the IEEE 1685 element this key is # borrowed from, but a format that numbers its entries from 1 says 1 rather # than being renumbered into a convention it does not follow. field "Flow Entry" 64 index="1..Entry Count" # `index=""`: it repeats, and nothing whatever about the indices is stated. # ONE occurrence draws, with a bare elision mark under it and no index on # either — the same ruling `present=""` gets for its caption. Two boxes would # assert a first and a last the author declined to state, and an invented # `[0] … [n-1]` would be the engine speaking for them. field "Vendor Counter" 32 index="" class=vendor
# No label written: the model records it ABSENT and the renderer falls back to # the id (`OMITTED-LABEL-RECORDING`) — never invent a caption. No `word=` either, so the row is the # default 32 bits. bitfield tlv numbering=msb0 # Compact form (the C bit-field convention): ONE whitespace-free token, items # comma-delimited. A name stays BARE here unless it contains whitespace, a # comma, a quote, a paren or `#` — the exact inverse of the classic form's # rule, because a comma-delimited element needs no quotes to terminate. field type:8,length:8,flags:8,rsvd:8 # A compact name containing SPACES must be quoted: the list terminates at the # first whitespace, so an unquoted spaced name cannot be told from the next # item. A name containing a COMMA cannot be written compactly at all. field "Scope Count":16,"Element Count":16 # Compact options are LINE-WIDE — one class covers all four items, exactly as # the classic form's single option set applies to its one field. All four # inherit `vendor`'s outline colour. Note what a class can NOT hand a field: # a DASH. Since `style=` left `field` (`STYLE-KEY-SCOPE`), `present=` is the # only source of one, and a class declaring `style=` reaches the legend and # nothing else. Line-wide is also why `index=` is NOT available here (`BITFIELD-REPETITION-CONSTRUCT`): # a line-wide range would say all four items repeat over the SAME indices, # which is not what any of them says. A repeated element is written in the # classic form, on a line of its own — `rec` above. field e1:8,e2:8,e3:8,e4:8 class=vendor field body:* # `*` is available in the compact form too
# lsb0 is the hardware-register convention: bit 0 is the LSB, so the ruler # runs N-1…0 left to right. `numbering=` relabels the RULER and nothing else — # placement is left to right in declaration order under either value — so a # register is written from its high end down, the way a datasheet prints it. # `fill=` and `stroke=` on the block are the DEFAULT cell fill and border; a # field's own fill=/stroke= wins. `stroke=` is NORMATIVE # (`STROKE-KEY-STATUS`) — an outline on a shape, and the whole line on an edge/bundle/ # threshold, which is SVG's own asymmetry borrowed unaltered. bitfield ctl "Exporter control register (0x40)" word=16 numbering=lsb0 fill=#fafaf9 stroke=#a8a29e # Option position is free on every directive (`OPTION-POSITION-PARSING`) — before the name or after. field class=reserved "RSVD" 4 field "MODE" 3 stroke=#b45309 # a field's own stroke= beats the block's field "INTERVAL" 8 fill=#dbeafe field "EN" 1 description="1 = exporter enabled"
